# NestJS RedisX

> Modular Redis toolkit for NestJS with plugin architecture. Provides two-tier caching (L1 memory + L2 Redis), distributed locks, rate limiting, a distributed circuit breaker, typed Pub/Sub, idempotency, Redis Streams, Prometheus metrics, and OpenTelemetry tracing. Supports both ioredis and node-redis drivers. TypeScript-first, zero external dependencies per plugin.

## Installation

Requirements: Node.js 18+, NestJS 10+, Redis 6+, TypeScript 5+.

Install core and your preferred Redis driver:

```bash
# ioredis
npm install @nestjs-redisx/core ioredis

# node-redis
npm install @nestjs-redisx/core redis
```

Install only the plugins you need:

```bash
npm install @nestjs-redisx/cache        # Two-tier caching
npm install @nestjs-redisx/locks        # Distributed locks
npm install @nestjs-redisx/rate-limit   # Rate limiting
npm install @nestjs-redisx/circuit-breaker # Distributed circuit breaker
npm install @nestjs-redisx/pubsub       # Typed Pub/Sub messaging
npm install @nestjs-redisx/idempotency  # Request deduplication
npm install @nestjs-redisx/streams      # Redis Streams
npm install @nestjs-redisx/metrics      # Prometheus metrics
npm install @nestjs-redisx/tracing      # OpenTelemetry tracing
```

## Core Module Configuration

### Synchronous Setup

```typescript
import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { RedisModule } from '@nestjs-redisx/core';
import { CachePlugin } from '@nestjs-redisx/cache';
import { LocksPlugin } from '@nestjs-redisx/locks';

@Module({
  imports: [
    RedisModule.forRoot({
      clients: {
        host: 'localhost',
        port: 6379,
        password: 'optional',
      },
      plugins: [
        new CachePlugin({
          l1: { maxSize: 1000, ttl: 60 },
          l2: { defaultTtl: 3600 },
        }),
        new LocksPlugin({ defaultTtl: 30000 }),
      ],
    }),
  ],
})
export class AppModule {}
```

### Asynchronous Setup (recommended for production)

```typescript
RedisModule.forRootAsync({
  imports: [ConfigModule],
  inject: [ConfigService],
  plugins: [new CachePlugin(), new LocksPlugin()],
  useFactory: (config: ConfigService) => ({
    clients: {
      host: config.get('REDIS_HOST'),
      port: config.get('REDIS_PORT'),
      password: config.get('REDIS_PASSWORD'),
    },
  }),
})
```

### Connection Types

Single instance (default):

```typescript
{ clients: { host: 'localhost', port: 6379 } }
```

Redis Cluster:

```typescript
{
  clients: {
    type: 'cluster',
    nodes: [
      { host: 'node1', port: 6379 },
      { host: 'node2', port: 6379 },
      { host: 'node3', port: 6379 },
    ],
  }
}
```

Redis Sentinel:

```typescript
{
  clients: {
    type: 'sentinel',
    sentinels: [
      { host: 'sentinel1', port: 26379 },
      { host: 'sentinel2', port: 26379 },
    ],
    name: 'mymaster',
  }
}
```

### Multiple Named Clients

```typescript
RedisModule.forRoot({
  clients: {
    default: { host: 'redis-primary', port: 6379 },
    cache: { host: 'redis-cache', port: 6380 },
    sessions: { host: 'redis-sessions', port: 6381 },
  },
})
```

Inject a specific client:

```typescript
import { InjectRedis, IRedisDriver } from '@nestjs-redisx/core';

@Injectable()
export class SessionService {
  constructor(@InjectRedis('sessions') private readonly redis: IRedisDriver) {}
}
```

### RedisService API

```typescript
import { RedisService } from '@nestjs-redisx/core';

@Injectable()
export class MyService {
  constructor(private readonly redis: RedisService) {}

  async example() {
    await this.redis.set('key', 'value');
    const val = await this.redis.get('key');
    await this.redis.del('key');
    await this.redis.expire('key', 3600);
    const exists = await this.redis.exists('key');
    // Access native client for advanced commands
    const client = this.redis.getClient();
  }
}
```

## Cache Plugin

Two-tier caching: L1 in-memory (per-instance) + L2 Redis (shared). Features: anti-stampede protection, stale-while-revalidate, tag-based invalidation, vary-by, custom serializers.

### CachePlugin Configuration

```typescript
new CachePlugin({
  l1: {
    enabled: true,
    maxSize: 1000,       // max entries in memory
    ttl: 60,             // L1 TTL in seconds
  },
  l2: {
    enabled: true,
    defaultTtl: 3600,    // L2 TTL in seconds
    keyPrefix: 'cache:',
  },
  stampede: {
    enabled: true,
    lockTimeout: 10000,  // ms to wait for lock during regeneration
  },
  staleIfError: {           // serve last-known-good when the loader FAILS
    enabled: false,          // opt-in (default: false)
    defaultWindow: 86400,    // seconds beyond normal expiry; always finite
    // shouldServe: (error) => !/404|410/.test(error.message),
  },
  swr: {
    enabled: false,
    staleTime: 300,      // seconds to serve stale while refreshing
  },
})
```

### @Cached Decorator

Works on any @Injectable() class method (services, controllers). Uses proxy-based wrapping — no HTTP context required.

```typescript
import { Cached } from '@nestjs-redisx/cache';

@Injectable()
export class UserService {
  // Basic caching with key template
  @Cached({ key: 'user:{0}', ttl: 300 })
  async findById(id: string): Promise<User> {
    return this.userRepository.findById(id);
  }

  // With tag-based invalidation
  @Cached({
    key: 'user:{0}',
    ttl: 300,
    tags: (id) => [`user:${id}`, 'users'],
  })
  async findByIdWithTags(id: string): Promise<User> {
    return this.userRepository.findById(id);
  }

  // Conditional caching
  @Cached({
    key: 'user:{0}',
    condition: (id) => id !== 'system',
    unless: (result) => result === null,
  })
  async findConditional(id: string): Promise<User | null> {
    return this.userRepository.findById(id);
  }

  // Multi-tenant with vary-by
  @Cached({
    key: 'products:{0}',
    varyBy: ['tenantId'],  // resolved from contextProvider (CLS/AsyncLocalStorage)
  })
  async findByCategory(category: string): Promise<Product[]> {
    return this.productRepository.findByCategory(category);
  }

  // Stale-while-revalidate
  @Cached({
    key: 'stats:dashboard',
    ttl: 60,
    swr: { enabled: true, staleTime: 300 },
  })
  async getDashboardStats(): Promise<DashboardStats> {
    return this.analyticsService.computeStats();
  }
}
```

Key template placeholders: `{0}`, `{1}`, etc. map to method argument positions.

### Cache Service API (programmatic)

```typescript
import { CACHE_SERVICE, ICacheService } from '@nestjs-redisx/cache';

@Injectable()
export class MyService {
  constructor(@Inject(CACHE_SERVICE) private readonly cache: ICacheService) {}

  async example() {
    // Get with loader (cache-aside pattern)
    const user = await this.cache.getOrSet(
      'user:123',
      () => this.db.findUser('123'),
      { ttl: 300, tags: ['users', 'user:123'] },
    );

    // Plain get (key only, no loader)
    const cached = await this.cache.get('user:123');

    // Manual set
    await this.cache.set('key', value, { ttl: 3600 });

    // Delete
    await this.cache.delete('key');

    // Invalidate by tags
    await this.cache.invalidateTags(['users']);
    await this.cache.invalidateTags(['user:123']);

    // Clear all cache
    await this.cache.clear();
  }
}
```

### @InvalidateTags Decorator

```typescript
@InvalidateTags({
  tags: (id: string) => [`user:${id}`, 'users'],
})
async updateUser(id: string, data: UpdateUserDto): Promise<User> {
  return this.userRepository.update(id, data);
}
```

### Cache Flow

1. Check L1 (memory) → hit returns in <1ms
2. Check L2 (Redis) → hit backfills L1, returns in <5ms
3. Miss → execute method, store in L2 + L1, return result
4. If stampede protection enabled: only one request regenerates per cluster — concurrent local requests share the in-flight promise, and other instances wait for the distributed lock and reuse the cached value
5. If SWR enabled: serve stale immediately, refresh in background

### Stale-If-Error

With `staleIfError` enabled, entries are physically retained for `window` seconds beyond their normal expiry (`keepUntil = ttl + staleTime + window`); between expiry and keepUntil the value is invisible to the success path (healthy loaders reload fresh data) and is served ONLY when the loader throws. `shouldServe(error)` filters which errors qualify (default: any — exclude 404/410-style "data is gone" errors to avoid serving dead data forever). Retries are lazy and request-driven (no background timer), coalesced by stampede protection. Every stale-on-error serve logs a warning and increments `redisx_cache_stale_if_error_served_total`. The window must be a finite number (fail-fast `CacheConfigError` otherwise) — for a practically infinite outage budget set an explicit large value. Per-call: `getOrSet(key, loader, { staleIfError: { enabled, window, shouldServe } })`; per-method: same object on `@Cached`. Entries of non-users keep exactly the previous TTL (zero blast radius). SIE is the availability policy; SWR is the freshness policy — independent toggles that compose.

## Locks Plugin

Redis-based distributed locks with automatic renewal, ownership validation, and configurable retry strategies.

### LocksPlugin Configuration

```typescript
new LocksPlugin({
  defaultTtl: 30000,       // lock TTL in ms
  retryDelay: 200,         // ms between retry attempts
  retryCount: 10,          // max retry attempts
  autoRenew: {
    enabled: true,
    interval: 10000,       // renewal interval in ms
  },
})
```

### @WithLock Decorator

```typescript
import { WithLock } from '@nestjs-redisx/locks';

@Injectable()
export class OrderService {
  @WithLock({ key: 'order:{0}', ttl: 30000 })
  async processOrder(orderId: string): Promise<Order> {
    // Only one instance processes this order at a time
    return this.doProcess(orderId);
  }
}
```

### Lock Service API (programmatic)

```typescript
import { LOCK_SERVICE, ILockService } from '@nestjs-redisx/locks';

@Injectable()
export class MyService {
  constructor(@Inject(LOCK_SERVICE) private readonly lockService: ILockService) {}

  async example() {
    const result = await this.lockService.withLock(
      'resource:123',
      async () => {
        // exclusive operation
        return await this.process();
      },
      { ttl: 30000, waitTimeout: 10000 },
    );
  }
}
```

## Rate Limit Plugin

Multiple algorithms for API protection: fixed window, sliding window, token bucket. All run as atomic Lua scripts in Redis.

### RateLimitPlugin Configuration

```typescript
new RateLimitPlugin({
  defaultAlgorithm: 'sliding-window',  // 'fixed-window' | 'sliding-window' | 'token-bucket'
  defaultPoints: 100,                   // max requests
  defaultDuration: 60,                  // time window in seconds
  keyPrefix: 'rl:',
})
```

### @RateLimit Decorator + Guard

```typescript
import { RateLimit } from '@nestjs-redisx/rate-limit';
import { RateLimitGuard } from '@nestjs-redisx/rate-limit';

@Controller('api')
@UseGuards(RateLimitGuard)
export class ApiController {
  @Get('data')
  @RateLimit({ points: 100, duration: 60 })
  getData() { }

  @Post('submit')
  @RateLimit({ points: 10, duration: 60, algorithm: 'token-bucket' })
  submit() { }
}
```

### Key Extraction

Default: by IP address. Custom:

```typescript
@RateLimit({
  points: 100,
  duration: 60,
  key: (ctx) => {
    const req = ctx.switchToHttp().getRequest();
    return req.user?.id ?? req.ip;
  },
})
```

### Skip Rate Limiting

Skipping is configured via the `skip` predicate on `@RateLimit` (there is no
separate `@SkipRateLimit` decorator):

```typescript
import { RateLimit } from '@nestjs-redisx/rate-limit';

@Get('health')
@RateLimit({ points: 100, duration: 60, skip: () => true })
healthCheck() { return { status: 'ok' }; }
```

### Response Headers

Rate limit responses include standard headers: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, `Retry-After` (on 429).

### Algorithms

Fixed Window: Simple counter per time window. Cheap but allows burst at window boundaries.
Sliding Window: Rolling window that smooths out bursts. Best for most APIs.
Token Bucket: Allows controlled bursts up to bucket capacity. Best for bursty workloads.

## Circuit Breaker Plugin

Distributed circuit breaker (closed / open / half-open) shared across all application instances via Redis. Fails fast while a dependency is down, probes it during recovery, and supports per-call fallbacks. All state transitions run as atomic Lua scripts; the state keys share a hash tag, so it is Redis Cluster safe.

### CircuitBreakerPlugin Configuration

```typescript
new CircuitBreakerPlugin({
  failureThreshold: 5,        // failures within windowMs that trip CLOSED -> OPEN
  windowMs: 10000,            // rolling failure window (ms)
  openDurationMs: 30000,      // cooldown before probing (ms)
  halfOpenMaxCalls: 1,        // concurrent probes allowed while HALF_OPEN
  successThreshold: 1,        // successful probes required to close
  probeTimeoutMs: 30000,      // reclaim a probe slot if its outcome is never recorded (default: openDurationMs)
  keyPrefix: 'cb:',
  errorPolicy: 'fail-closed', // 'fail-open' runs the call when the STATE STORE is unavailable
})
```

All numeric knobs are validated (integers >= 1; successThreshold <= halfOpenMaxCalls) — an invalid config throws InvalidCircuitBreakerConfigError at bootstrap and on per-call overrides.

### @WithCircuitBreaker Decorator

Proxy-based — works on any @Injectable() method, not just controllers.

```typescript
import { WithCircuitBreaker } from '@nestjs-redisx/circuit-breaker';

@Injectable()
export class PaymentsService {
  @WithCircuitBreaker({ key: 'stripe', failureThreshold: 5, openDurationMs: 30000 })
  async charge(dto: ChargeDto) { return this.stripe.charge(dto); }

  // Key interpolation from arguments ({0}, {0.id}) + fallback while OPEN
  @WithCircuitBreaker({ key: 'users-api:{0}', fallback: (id) => ({ id, cached: true }) })
  async getUser(id: string) { return this.api.getUser(id); }

  // Resolve to undefined instead of throwing while OPEN
  @WithCircuitBreaker({ key: 'analytics', onOpen: 'skip' })
  async track(event: AnalyticsEvent) { /* ... */ }

  // Bypass the breaker entirely for trusted calls (no state read or recorded)
  @WithCircuitBreaker({ key: 'api', skip: (req) => req.internal === true })
  async call(req: ApiRequest) { /* ... */ }
}
```

### Service API

```typescript
import { CIRCUIT_BREAKER_SERVICE, ICircuitBreakerService } from '@nestjs-redisx/circuit-breaker';

const user = await breaker.execute('users-api', () => api.getUser(id), {
  fallback: () => cachedUser, // served instead of throwing while OPEN
});

await breaker.recordSuccess('users-api'); // manual recording (e.g. from a health probe)
await breaker.recordFailure('users-api');
const { state, failuresInWindow } = await breaker.getState('users-api'); // non-mutating
await breaker.reset('users-api'); // force back to CLOSED
```

### States

CLOSED: calls run; failures are counted over a rolling `windowMs`; reaching `failureThreshold` trips to OPEN.
OPEN: calls are rejected immediately (CircuitBreakerOpenError or the fallback); after `openDurationMs` the next request probes.
HALF_OPEN: up to `halfOpenMaxCalls` concurrent probes; `successThreshold` successes close the breaker, any probe failure re-opens it. A probe left unresolved longer than `probeTimeoutMs` loses its slot automatically (crash-safe recovery).

`errorPolicy` governs STATE STORE failures only: 'fail-open' runs the guarded call anyway, 'fail-closed' (default) throws CircuitBreakerStoreError. The manual API (recordSuccess/recordFailure/getState/reset) is always strict. The pure state machine (`CircuitBreakerState`) is exported for hermetic unit tests — every time-dependent method takes an explicit `now`.

## Pub/Sub Plugin

Typed Redis Pub/Sub: publish/subscribe with JSON payloads, pattern subscriptions, a @Subscribe decorator with automatic discovery, and a DEDICATED subscriber connection managed for you (a Redis connection in subscriber mode cannot execute regular commands, so the plugin clones one from your named client automatically as `<client>:pubsub-subscriber`).

### PubSubPlugin Configuration

```typescript
new PubSubPlugin({
  client: 'default',   // named Redis client used for publishing
  channelPrefix: '',   // optional namespace applied to every channel/pattern
                       // (empty by default for interop with non-RedisX publishers)
})
```

### @Subscribe Decorator

Handler methods on any @Injectable() provider are auto-discovered on startup:

```typescript
import { Subscribe, IPubSubMessage } from '@nestjs-redisx/pubsub';

@Injectable()
export class UserEvents {
  @Subscribe('user.created') // exact channel
  onCreated(message: IPubSubMessage<{ id: string }>) {
    console.log(message.channel, message.data.id);
  }

  @Subscribe({ pattern: 'user.*' }) // Redis glob pattern (*, ?, [..])
  onAnyUserEvent(message: IPubSubMessage) {
    console.log(message.pattern, message.channel, message.data);
  }
}
```

### Service API

```typescript
import { PUBSUB_SERVICE, IPubSubService } from '@nestjs-redisx/pubsub';

const receivers = await pubsub.publish('user.created', { id: '42' }); // JSON-serialized
const sub = await pubsub.subscribe<UserCreated>('user.created', (msg) => {
  console.log(msg.channel, msg.data, msg.raw);
});
await sub.unsubscribe(); // last handler releases the Redis subscription
```

Multiple handlers per channel multiplex over ONE Redis subscription. Handler errors are logged, never propagated into the dispatch loop. Non-JSON payloads from other systems are delivered with `data` = raw string (fail-open interop). All subscriptions are cleaned up on shutdown. Pub/Sub is fire-and-forget (no persistence, no replay, at-most-once) — use the Streams plugin when you need durable delivery.

Note: with the node-redis driver, Pub/Sub is supported on single-node connections; use ioredis for Pub/Sub over Cluster/Sentinel topologies.

## Idempotency Plugin

Request deduplication for payments, order creation, and mutations. Ensures operations execute exactly once even when clients retry.

### IdempotencyPlugin Configuration

```typescript
new IdempotencyPlugin({
  headerName: 'Idempotency-Key',  // HTTP header name
  defaultTtl: 86400,               // response cache TTL in seconds (24h)
  validateFingerprint: true,        // detect mismatched requests with same key
})
```

### @Idempotent Decorator

```typescript
import { Idempotent } from '@nestjs-redisx/idempotency';

@Controller('payments')
export class PaymentsController {
  @Post()
  @Idempotent({ ttl: 86400, validateFingerprint: true })
  async createPayment(@Body() dto: CreatePaymentDto): Promise<Payment> {
    return this.paymentService.process(dto);
  }
}
```

### How It Works

1. Client sends request with `Idempotency-Key: <unique-key>` header
2. First request: executes handler, caches response in Redis (the record fields and TTL are written in ONE atomic Lua script)
3. Duplicate request (same key): returns cached response without executing handler
4. Concurrent request (same key, first still processing): waits for first to complete, returns same result
5. Mismatched request (same key, different body): returns 422 error if fingerprinting enabled

The default fingerprint serializes the body (and query, when included) CANONICALLY — object keys sorted recursively — so two semantically identical bodies with different key order produce the same fingerprint (no false 422 from field ordering; array order is preserved). Records expire after `defaultTtl`: a retry AFTER expiry is indistinguishable from a new request and executes again — size the TTL past your clients' retry horizon and keep the durable "was this done" answer in your database for money movement.

## Streams Plugin

Redis Streams with consumer groups, dead letter queues, batch processing, and automatic retry with exponential backoff.

### StreamsPlugin Configuration

```typescript
new StreamsPlugin({
  consumer: {
    groupName: 'my-service',
    consumerName: 'instance-1',
    blockTimeout: 5000,        // ms to block waiting for messages
    batchSize: 10,             // messages per read
    maxRetries: 3,             // retries before DLQ
  },
})
```

### Publishing Messages

```typescript
import { STREAM_PRODUCER, IStreamProducer } from '@nestjs-redisx/streams';

@Injectable()
export class OrderService {
  constructor(@Inject(STREAM_PRODUCER) private readonly streams: IStreamProducer) {}

  async createOrder(order: Order) {
    await this.streams.publish('orders', {
      type: 'order.created',
      payload: order,
    });
  }

  async publishBatch(events: Event[]) {
    await this.streams.publishBatch('events', events);
  }
}
```

### Consuming Messages

```typescript
import { StreamConsumer } from '@nestjs-redisx/streams';

@Injectable()
export class OrderProcessor {
  @StreamConsumer({
    stream: 'orders',
    group: 'processor',
    consumer: 'worker-1',
  })
  async handleOrder(message: StreamMessage) {
    const order = message.data;
    await this.process(order);
    // Message auto-acknowledged on success
    // Auto-retried on error with exponential backoff
    // Moved to DLQ after maxRetries
  }
}
```

## Metrics Plugin

Prometheus-compatible metrics for all Redis operations and plugin activity.

### MetricsPlugin Configuration

```typescript
new MetricsPlugin({
  endpoint: '/metrics',        // HTTP endpoint path
  prefix: 'redisx_',          // metric name prefix
  defaultLabels: { app: 'my-service' },
})
```

### Available Metrics

Command metrics: `commands_total`, `command_duration_seconds`, `connections_active`, `errors_total`.
Cache metrics: `cache_hits_total`, `cache_misses_total`, `cache_hit_ratio`, `cache_size`, `cache_stampede_prevented_total`.
Lock metrics: `lock_acquisitions_total`, `lock_wait_duration_seconds`, `lock_hold_duration_seconds`, `locks_active`.
Rate limit metrics: `ratelimit_requests_total` (with status label: allowed/rejected).
Stream metrics: `stream_messages_published_total`, `stream_messages_consumed_total`, `stream_processing_duration_seconds`.
Idempotency metrics: `idempotency_requests_total` (with status: new/replay/conflict).

## Tracing Plugin

OpenTelemetry distributed tracing for Redis operations.

### TracingPlugin Configuration

```typescript
new TracingPlugin({
  serviceName: 'my-service',
  exporter: {
    type: 'otlp',              // 'otlp' | 'jaeger' | 'zipkin' | 'console'
    endpoint: 'http://collector:4318/v1/traces',
  },
  sampling: {
    strategy: 'parent',        // 'always' | 'never' | 'ratio' | 'parent' (default: 'parent')
    ratio: 0.1,                // root-span ratio for 'ratio' and 'parent'
  },
  traceRedisCommands: true,    // native redis.<COMMAND> spans (default: true)
  spans: { includeArgs: false, includeResult: false, maxArgLength: 100, excludeCommands: [] },
})
```

Sampling defaults to parent-based (OTel SDK convention): Redis spans follow the sampling decision of the request trace they belong to; root spans fall back to `ratio`. For keep-all-errors / keep-slow policies use tail sampling in the OpenTelemetry Collector — RedisX spans carry ERROR status and recorded exceptions.

### Automatic Redis Command Spans

Every command executed through RedisX drivers is wrapped natively in a `redis.<COMMAND>` CLIENT span (no external instrumentation package) covering all named clients and runtime-created connections. Spans parent onto the active OpenTelemetry context, so with standard HTTP instrumentation a cache lookup appears inside the HTTP request's trace. `spans.excludeCommands` skips commands; `includeArgs`/`includeResult` gate payload attributes (truncated to `maxArgLength`). Note: the plugin registers a NodeTracerProvider; if you bootstrap your own OTel SDK first, your SDK owns the pipeline and the plugin's exporter/sampling options are inert.

### Span Attributes

Each Redis command span includes: `db.system: "redis"`, `db.operation`, `db.statement`, `redisx.client`, `redisx.duration_ms`, and optional `db.statement.args` / `db.statement.result`. Plugin-level spans (cache/locks/rate-limit) add `redisx.plugin`, `redisx.cache.hit` (boolean).

## Testing Utilities

`@nestjs-redisx/testing` provides an in-memory Redis driver so you can unit-test code that uses the cache, locks, rate-limit, circuit-breaker, pubsub, idempotency, and streams plugins **without a running Redis**. The plugins run their real production code — including their Lua scripts, stream consumer groups, and Pub/Sub subscriptions — against an in-memory keyspace. Install it as a devDependency: `npm install -D @nestjs-redisx/testing`.

### RedisTestingModule (recommended)

```typescript
import { Test } from '@nestjs/testing';
import { RedisTestingModule } from '@nestjs-redisx/testing';
import { CachePlugin, CACHE_SERVICE, ICacheService } from '@nestjs-redisx/cache';

const app = await Test.createTestingModule({
  imports: [RedisTestingModule.forRoot({ plugins: [new CachePlugin()] })],
}).compile();
await app.init();
const cache = app.get<ICacheService>(CACHE_SERVICE);
// cache.getOrSet(...) runs the real cache code against the in-memory driver
```

`RedisTestingModule.forRoot(options?)` and `RedisTestingModule.forRootAsync(options)` wrap `RedisModule` and force `global.driver = 'memory'`. `clients` is optional (the driver never connects).

### global.driver option

Alternatively configure `RedisModule` directly. Importing `@nestjs-redisx/testing` registers the `'memory'` driver as a side effect:

```typescript
import '@nestjs-redisx/testing';
import { RedisModule } from '@nestjs-redisx/core';

RedisModule.forRoot({
  clients: { type: 'single', host: 'localhost', port: 6379 }, // host/port ignored
  global: { driver: 'memory' },
  plugins: [/* ... */],
});
```

`registerMemoryDriver()` can be called explicitly (idempotent) to register the driver with the core registry.

### Supported commands

Strings (`GET`/`SET`/`SETEX`/`SETNX`/`APPEND`/`STRLEN`/`INCR`/`INCRBY`/`DECR`/`DECRBY`/`MGET`/`MSET`), keys & TTL (`DEL`/`UNLINK`/`EXISTS`/`EXPIRE`/`PEXPIRE`/`EXPIREAT`/`PEXPIREAT`/`PERSIST`/`TTL`/`PTTL`/`TYPE`/`KEYS`/`SCAN`), hashes (`HSET`/`HMSET`/`HGET`/`HMGET`/`HGETALL`/`HDEL`/`HEXISTS`/`HLEN`/`HKEYS`/`HVALS`/`HINCRBY`), sets (`SADD`/`SREM`/`SMEMBERS`/`SISMEMBER`/`SCARD`), sorted sets (`ZADD`/`ZREM`/`ZCARD`/`ZSCORE`/`ZRANGE`/`ZRANGEBYSCORE`/`ZREMRANGEBYSCORE`/`ZCOUNT`), lists (`LPUSH`/`RPUSH`/`LPOP`/`RPOP`/`LLEN`/`LRANGE`/`LINDEX`/`LREM`), streams (`XADD`/`XLEN`/`XRANGE`/`XREVRANGE`/`XDEL`/`XTRIM`/`XINFO STREAM`/`XGROUP`/`XREADGROUP`/`XREAD`/`XACK`/`XPENDING`/`XCLAIM` with real consumer-group + PEL semantics), scripting (`EVAL`/`EVALSHA`/`SCRIPT LOAD`), pub/sub (`PUBLISH`/`SUBSCRIBE`/`UNSUBSCRIBE`/`PSUBSCRIBE`/`PUNSUBSCRIBE` via a process-wide bus with glob pattern matching), server (`PING`/`DBSIZE`/`FLUSHDB`/`FLUSHALL`). TTL uses lazy expiry. A built-in Lua interpreter runs the plugins' atomic scripts. Blocking `XREADGROUP`/`XREAD` returns promptly (no real blocking).

### Seeding & inspecting state

Cast the injected `REDIS_DRIVER` to `MemoryRedisAdapter` and call `getStore()` to reach the in-memory `MemoryStore` (`writeString`, `read`, `flush`, `keys`, TTL helpers) for arranging or resetting state in tests.

### Exports & limitations

Exports: `RedisTestingModule`, `registerMemoryDriver`, `MemoryRedisAdapter`, `MemoryStore`, `CommandExecutor`, `LuaInterpreter`, `MEMORY_DRIVER_TYPE`, `IMemoryDriverOptions`, and errors `MemoryDriverError` / `LuaExecutionError` / `WrongTypeError`. Limitations: single-node semantics only (no cluster cross-slot); Pub/Sub is a process-wide bus with single-node semantics; blocking reads return promptly; unsupported commands or Lua constructs fail loudly rather than returning wrong results; it is a correctness tool, not a performance simulator.

## Complete API Reference

Every public service method, grouped by injection token. Inject the token to use the programmatic API (decorators wrap these same services).

### Cache — `CACHE_SERVICE` (`ICacheService`)

- `get<T>(key: string): Promise<T | null>` — read a value (L1 then L2); null on miss. Reads fail open.
- `set<T>(key: string, value: T, options?: CacheSetOptions): Promise<void>` — write a value (TTL, tags, strategy). Writes fail closed.
- `getOrSet<T>(key: string, loader: () => Promise<T>, options?: CacheGetOrSetOptions): Promise<T>` — return cached value or run loader, cache and return it (stampede-protected).
- `delete(key: string): Promise<boolean>` — delete one key from L1+L2.
- `deleteMany(keys: string[]): Promise<number>` — delete many keys; returns count removed.
- `getMany<T>(keys: string[]): Promise<Array<T | null>>` — batch read; returns an array aligned to input keys.
- `setMany<T>(entries): Promise<void>` — batch write multiple entries.
- `has(key: string): Promise<boolean>` — existence check.
- `ttl(key: string): Promise<number>` — remaining TTL in seconds (-1 no expiry, -2 missing).
- `clear(): Promise<void>` — clear all cache entries.
- `invalidateTag(tag: string): Promise<number>` — invalidate all keys carrying a tag; returns count. Throws `TagInvalidationError` on failure.
- `invalidateTags(tags: string[]): Promise<number>` — invalidate keys for multiple tags.
- `getKeysByTag(tag: string): Promise<string[]>` — list keys associated with a tag.
- `invalidateByPattern(pattern: string): Promise<number>` — invalidate keys matching a glob pattern.
- `getStats(): Promise<CacheStats>` — hit/miss/size statistics (async).
- `wrap<T>(...)` — helper that wraps a function call with getOrSet semantics.

Key chars are restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9-_:.]` (else `CacheKeyError`); tags are lowercase. `stampede.fallback` ('load' | 'error' | 'null', default 'load') controls behavior when stampede protection times out.

Standalone helpers: `hashKey(value)` hashes any JSON-serializable value into a stable 16-hex cache-key segment — the SAME frozen algorithm `@Cached` uses for auto-generated keys (recursive key-sorted serialization + SHA-256/16), so `{a:1,b:2}` and `{b:2,a:1}` produce the same key; `stableStringify(value)` exposes the canonical serialization itself; `KeyBuilder.hashStable(obj)` adds the same hash as a fluent-builder segment. The algorithm is frozen (changing it would invalidate derived keys); it is for cache keys, not identity/security. `KeyBuilder.hash()` is DEPRECATED (key-order-sensitive, 32-bit, collision-prone) — its output is unchanged for backward compatibility and it will be removed in 2.0.

### Locks — `LOCK_SERVICE` (`ILockService`)

- `acquire(key: string, options?: ILockOptions): Promise<ILock>` — acquire with retry/backoff; throws `LockAcquisitionError` on timeout. `options.waitTimeout` caps total wait time.
- `tryAcquire(key: string, options?: ILockOptions): Promise<ILock | null>` — single attempt; null if not acquired.
- `withLock<T>(key: string, fn: () => Promise<T>, options?: ILockOptions): Promise<T>` — run fn while holding the lock, auto-released.
- `isLocked(key: string): Promise<boolean>` — whether the key is currently locked.
- `forceRelease(key: string): Promise<boolean>` — release without ownership check.
- Lock entity: `release()`, `extend(ttl)`, `isHeld()`, `stopAutoRenew()`, `isAutoRenewing`. Auto-renew is best-effort and logs a warning (and flips `isAutoRenewing` to false) if it can no longer extend.

### Rate Limit — `RATE_LIMIT_SERVICE` (`IRateLimitService`)

- `check(key: string, config?: IRateLimitConfig): Promise<IRateLimitResult>` — consume one point; result has allowed/limit/remaining/reset/retryAfter.
- `peek(key: string, config?: IRateLimitConfig): Promise<IRateLimitResult>` — read current state WITHOUT consuming (accurate for fixed-window, sliding-window, and token-bucket).
- `getState(key: string, config?: IRateLimitConfig): Promise<IRateLimitState>` — human-readable state (current/limit/remaining/resetAt).
- `reset(key: string): Promise<void>` — clear the limit for a key (all algorithm variants).

The `@RateLimit` decorator binds `RateLimitGuard`; the guard consumes at most one point per request even if bound more than once.

### Circuit Breaker — `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_SERVICE` (`ICircuitBreakerService`)

- `execute<T>(key: string, fn: () => Promise<T>, options?: ICircuitBreakerExecuteOptions<T>): Promise<T>` — run `fn` guarded by the breaker; records success on resolve and failure on throw. While OPEN, returns `options.fallback()` if provided, otherwise throws `options.errorFactory`/plugin `errorFactory` or `CircuitBreakerOpenError`.
- `recordSuccess(key: string, options?: ICircuitBreakerOptions): Promise<ICircuitSnapshot>` — manually record a success (e.g. from a health probe); returns the resulting snapshot.
- `recordFailure(key: string, options?: ICircuitBreakerOptions): Promise<ICircuitSnapshot>` — manually record a failure; returns the resulting snapshot.
- `getState(key: string, options?: ICircuitBreakerOptions): Promise<ICircuitSnapshot>` — read the committed state (closed/open/half-open) without mutating it.
- `reset(key: string): Promise<void>` — return the circuit to CLOSED and clear all state.

States: CLOSED counts failures in a rolling `windowMs`; at `failureThreshold` it trips to OPEN for `openDurationMs`; the next request then flips to HALF_OPEN, allowing up to `halfOpenMaxCalls` probes (a probe unresolved longer than `probeTimeoutMs`, default `openDurationMs`, has its slot reclaimed), and `successThreshold` successes close it (any probe failure re-opens). The `@WithCircuitBreaker` decorator is proxy-based and works on any Injectable method. `errorPolicy` ('fail-open' | 'fail-closed', default 'fail-closed') governs behavior when the state store is unavailable.

### Pub/Sub — `PUBSUB_SERVICE` (`IPubSubService`)

- `publish<T>(channel: string, data: T): Promise<number>` — publish a JSON-serialized payload to a channel; returns the number of subscribers that received it. Throws `PubSubPublishError` on serialization or PUBLISH failure.
- `subscribe<T>(channel: string, handler: PubSubMessageHandler<T>): Promise<IPubSubSubscription>` — register a handler for a channel; multiple handlers multiplex over one Redis subscription. Throws `PubSubSubscribeError` on SUBSCRIBE failure.
- `psubscribe<T>(pattern: string, handler: PubSubMessageHandler<T>): Promise<IPubSubSubscription>` — register a handler for a Redis glob pattern (`*`, `?`, `[..]`); messages carry both pattern and concrete channel.
- `unsubscribeAll(): Promise<void>` — remove ALL handlers and release every Redis subscription (called automatically on module destroy).
- `getSubscriptions(): IPubSubSubscriptionsSnapshot` — non-mutating snapshot of logical channels and patterns with active handlers (for monitoring/health).

`IPubSubMessage` carries `channel` (logical name without prefix), `pattern?`, `data` (deserialized; falls back to the raw string when JSON parsing fails), and `raw`. `IPubSubSubscription.unsubscribe()` removes one handler; the Redis subscription is released with the last handler. The `@Subscribe` decorator is discovery-based (channels and patterns). Delivery is at-most-once, fire-and-forget.

### Idempotency — `IDEMPOTENCY_SERVICE` (`IIdempotencyService`)

- `checkAndLock(key: string, fingerprint: string, options?: IIdempotencyOptions): Promise<IIdempotencyCheckResult>` — atomically reserve a new key or report processing/completed/failed/fingerprint_mismatch.
- `complete(key: string, response: IIdempotencyResponse, options?: IIdempotencyOptions): Promise<void>` — store a successful response for replay (TTL = defaultTtl).
- `fail(key: string, error: string, options?: IIdempotencyOptions): Promise<void>` — mark failed (short TTL = lockTimeout) so a retry is allowed after the window; pass `fingerprint` so replays keep matching.
- `get(key: string): Promise<IIdempotencyRecord | null>` — read the stored record.
- `delete(key: string): Promise<boolean>` — remove a record.

Errors map to HTTP via the built-in filter: fingerprint mismatch → 422, previous-failed/timeout/vanished-in-flight → 409, missing key → 400; the body carries a machine-readable `code` (e.g. IDEMPOTENCY_TIMEOUT vs IDEMPOTENCY_FAILED) so clients can distinguish the 409 variants. `errorPolicy` ('fail-open' | 'fail-closed', default 'fail-closed') decides behavior when the store is unavailable; fail-open trades the idempotency guarantee for availability (duplicates are possible while the store is down). `lockTimeout` is a STALENESS threshold, not the record lifetime: processing records are retained for 2x lockTimeout, so once the first attempt exceeds lockTimeout without completing, the next request or waiter takes the lock over ATOMICALLY inside the Lua script and executes the handler itself. The interceptor engages at most once per request even when bound multiple times (global registration + @Idempotent is safe; never add @UseInterceptors(IdempotencyInterceptor) manually — @Idempotent already includes it). `validateFingerprint: false` (plugin or per-@Idempotent) replays a reused key without comparing request contents.

### Streams Producer — `STREAM_PRODUCER` (`IStreamProducer`)

- `publish<T>(stream: string, data: T, options?: IPublishOptions): Promise<string>` — append one message; returns its id.
- `publishBatch<T>(stream: string, messages: T[], options?: IPublishOptions): Promise<string[]>` — append many messages.
- `getStreamInfo(stream: string): Promise<IStreamInfo>` — length, first/last entry, group count.
- `trim(stream: string, maxLen: number): Promise<number>` — trim a stream to maxLen on demand.

`trim` config controls trimming on publish (`trim.enabled: false` = keep-all); `producer.autoCreate: false` sets NOMKSTREAM.

### Streams Consumer — `STREAM_CONSUMER` (`IStreamConsumer`)

- `consume<T>(stream, group, consumer, handler: MessageHandler<T>, options?: IConsumeOptions): IConsumerHandle` — start consuming; handler return = ack, throw = retry/DLQ.
- `stop(handle: IConsumerHandle): Promise<void>` — stop a consumer.
- `createGroup(stream: string, group: string, startId?: string): Promise<void>` — create a consumer group.
- `getPending(stream: string, group: string): Promise<IPendingInfo>` — pending (unacked) message info.
- `claimIdle<T>(stream, group, consumer, minIdleTime): Promise<IStreamMessage<T>[]>` — on-demand claim of idle messages. Consumers also auto-claim in the background (`consumer.claimIdleTimeout`, default 30000ms; 0 disables).

### Metrics — `METRICS_SERVICE` (`IMetricsService`)

- `incrementCounter(name, labels?, value?): void` — increment a counter.
- `observeHistogram(name, value, labels?): void` — record a histogram observation.
- `startTimer(name, labels?): () => number` — start a timer; call the returned fn to record elapsed seconds.
- `setGauge(name, value, labels?): void` / `incrementGauge(name, labels?, value?): void` / `decrementGauge(name, labels?, value?): void` — gauge operations.
- `registerCounter(name, help, labelNames?): void` / `registerHistogram(name, help, labelNames?, buckets?): void` / `registerGauge(name, help, labelNames?): void` — register custom metrics.
- `getMetrics(): Promise<string>` — Prometheus exposition text.
- `getMetricsJson(): Promise<IMetricsJson[]>` — metrics as JSON.

Options: `histogramBuckets`, `endpoint`.

### Tracing — `TRACING_SERVICE` (`ITracingService`)

- `startSpan(name: string, options?: ISpanOptions): ISpan` — start a span (caller ends it).
- `withSpan<T>(name, fn: () => T | Promise<T>, options?: ISpanOptions): Promise<T>` — run fn within a span, auto-ended.
- `getCurrentSpan(): ISpan | undefined` — the active span, if any.
- `addEvent(name, attributes?): void` — add an event to the current span.
- `setAttribute(key, value): void` — set an attribute on the current span.
- `recordException(error: Error): void` — record an exception on the current span.

Default `serviceName` is `'nestjs-redisx'`.

## Common Recipes

### Payment Processing (Idempotency + Locks)

```typescript
@Controller('payments')
export class PaymentsController {
  @Post()
  @Idempotent({ ttl: 86400, validateFingerprint: true })
  async createPayment(@Body() dto: CreatePaymentDto) {
    return this.paymentService.processPayment(dto);
  }
}

@Injectable()
export class PaymentService {
  constructor(@Inject(LOCK_SERVICE) private readonly lockService: ILockService) {}

  async processPayment(dto: CreatePaymentDto) {
    return this.lockService.withLock(`order:${dto.orderId}`, async () => {
      const existing = await this.repo.findByOrderId(dto.orderId);
      if (existing?.status === 'completed') return existing;

      const payment = await this.repo.create(dto);
      const result = await this.gateway.charge(dto);
      await this.repo.update(payment.id, { status: 'completed' });
      return payment;
    });
  }
}
```

### API Rate Limiting (multi-tier)

```typescript
// Global: 1000 req/min for all users
@UseGuards(RateLimitGuard)
@RateLimit({ points: 1000, duration: 60 })
@Controller('api')
export class ApiController {

  // Endpoint-specific: 10 req/min for expensive operations
  @Post('export')
  @RateLimit({ points: 10, duration: 60 })
  exportData() { }

  // Per-user rate limiting
  @Get('data')
  @RateLimit({
    points: 100,
    duration: 60,
    key: (ctx) => `user:${ctx.switchToHttp().getRequest().user.id}`,
  })
  getData() { }
}
```

### Background Jobs (Streams)

```typescript
// Producer
@Injectable()
export class JobService {
  constructor(@Inject(STREAM_PRODUCER) private streams: IStreamProducer) {}

  async enqueue(job: Job) {
    await this.streams.publish('jobs', { type: job.type, payload: job.data });
  }
}

// Consumer
@Injectable()
export class JobWorker {
  @StreamConsumer({ stream: 'jobs', group: 'workers' })
  async process(message: StreamMessage) {
    switch (message.data.type) {
      case 'email': await this.sendEmail(message.data.payload); break;
      case 'report': await this.generateReport(message.data.payload); break;
    }
  }
}
```

## Plugin Decision Matrix

| Scenario | Plugin |
|----------|--------|
| Slow database queries | Cache |
| Duplicate form submissions | Idempotency |
| Payment processing | Idempotency + Locks |
| Cron job on multiple instances | Locks |
| API abuse protection | Rate Limit |
| Login brute force | Rate Limit |
| Flaky third-party API | Circuit Breaker |
| Payment gateway outages | Circuit Breaker + fallback |
| Background job processing | Streams |
| Event-driven architecture | Streams |
| Production monitoring | Metrics |
| Request tracing | Tracing |

## Key Architecture Decisions

- **Proxy-based decorators**: @Cached, @WithLock, @WithCircuitBreaker work on any @Injectable() method, not just controllers. NestJS Interceptors only work on controller methods, so RedisX uses immediate method wrapping with lazy service injection.
- **Plugin isolation**: Each plugin is a self-contained NestJS module. Import only what you need.
- **Driver abstraction**: Both ioredis and node-redis supported through adapter pattern. Switch without code changes.
- **Atomic operations**: Rate limiting, locks, idempotency, and the circuit breaker use Lua scripts for atomicity.
- **No external dependencies**: Each plugin has zero npm dependencies beyond NestJS and the Redis driver.
- **Global module**: RedisModule is global — import once in AppModule, inject anywhere.
- **Composition over inheritance**: No base classes required. Decorators and services compose freely.

## Deployment Topologies

Single: Development and small apps. No HA.
Sentinel: Production HA. Automatic failover ~30s. Vertical scaling.
Cluster: Horizontal scaling with 16384 hash slots. Use `{hash_tag}` to co-locate keys.
